title: How to Check Network Adapter Status
overview: This article supports the Check Network Adapter Status step in the VPN Connectivity Troubleshooting (Windows) workflow. It explains how to identify the status of physical and VPN network adapters without making unnecessary configuration changes.
checklist: Save open work and confirm you are working on the intended device.
Open Network Connections by pressing Windows + R, typing ncpa.cpl, and selecting OK.
Identify the active physical network adapter and, if applicable, the VPN adapter used by your organization.
Do not change unfamiliar, virtual machine, or organization-managed adapters.
If the expected adapter is disabled, record its name and status before enabling it so the troubleshooting workflow can accurately document the change.
Be aware that enabling a disabled adapter changes the system's network state and may require reconnecting to the network or VPN.
common_indicators: The expected network adapter is enabled and connected.
related_topics: Enable or Disable a Network Adapter
